title:
Climate Talks Stall in Turkey.
Zelensky Calls Putin a Killer.
Wall Street Slides Into Correction.
subject: Climate Talks Stall in Turkey. Zelensky Calls Putin a Killer. Wall Street Slides Into Correction.
preview_text: A COP31 standoff, a war of words over Putin, a tech rout, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: COP31 talks in Turkey deadlock over fossil fuels, Zelensky answers Trump on Putin and an AI sell-off drags Wall Street into a correction.
contents_extra: Trump's threat to keep data centers at home, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: COP31 Climate Talks Run Into Overtime as Countries Clash Over Fossil Fuels
paragraphs: The BBC reports COP31 negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, ran through the night in deadlock. A group led by France and Panama pushed back against a draft with no reference to cutting fossil fuel demand. The Africa Group is fighting for more adaptation money. A new and potentially final agreement is expected on Saturday, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports a second, shorter draft dropped any mention of fossil fuels and weakened electrification goals. Eight countries called for a clear transition away from fossil fuels to be restored. Several insiders said Saudi Arabia played an obstructive role, the paper reports. Talks president Chris Bowen said no one had told him to give up and go home.

stories.title: Zelensky Calls Putin a Killer After Trump Describes Him as a Friend
paragraphs: The BBC reports President Volodymyr Zelensky called Vladimir Putin a "killer" in an interview with CNN. He was answering Donald Trump, who called the Russian leader his "friend" in China this week. Zelensky said such talk meant Putin "doesn't feel enough pressure". Officials said overnight strikes on Kryvyi Rih killed two people, including a boy.

The Guardian reports Trump told a White House press conference he has "fantastic relationships" with Putin and Xi Jinping. Asked whether Putin is a friend to America, Trump said he could not speak to that. The BBC says Trump also said Putin would love to end the war. Poland said a Russian cruise missile violated its airspace on Friday.

photo.alt: Ukrainian flag on a pole in Lviv, file photo

stories.title: Wall Street Slides Into a Correction as the AI Sell-Off Deepens
paragraphs: The BBC reports the S&P 500 closed down 3.7% on Friday, while the Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.3% and the Dow fell 1.9%. The S&P 500 and the Dow were pushed into correction territory. That means trading 10% or more below a recent high. Anthropic shares closed down 8.5%, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports the Nasdaq erased all its gains for 2026 and closed 5% below its Jan. 1 level. Citing the Wall Street Journal, it says the index shed some $4tn in market value this week. Nvidia fell 14% on Friday, the paper says. Saxo strategist Neil Wilson described "just relentless selling in tech".

deep_dive.title: Why Trump Wants American Data Centers Kept at Home
paragraphs: The BBC reports Donald Trump said he will ban US companies from building AI data centres overseas. He threatened a "tremendous tax" on firms that do so. Trump gave little detail and said his cabinet was hearing the idea for the first time. It remains unclear how such a policy would be enforced, the BBC says.

CNBC reports Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle have already built data centers abroad. Cloud providers want facilities near clients, sometimes to meet regulatory rules. Trump said firms "can" keep building abroad but would face a tremendous tax. A CNBC survey found 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of home.

CNBC reports European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde wants EU public funds to take the first losses on chip plants and data centers. She warned that dependence on foreign technology leaves Europe exposed. Separately, Trump singled out a Google project in Finland, the BBC says. Google announced a EUR 13bn AI investment there in September.

CNBC reports US data center construction costs rose 13% this year, more than twice the global rate, citing Turner and Townsend. Demand outran powered land and labor, the report found. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to CNBC. The BBC says Canada is offering itself as an alternative location.

trivia.question: What share of energy from electricity by 2035 is being urged at COP31, according to the Guardian?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 35%. The Guardian reports countries are being urged to derive 35% of final energy use from electricity by 2035.

poll.question: Should a climate deal name fossil fuels directly?

World view: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill a rapper near Copenhagen, the BBC reports Moscow called the allegations unsubstantiated.
South Africa's ANC races to strike city coalition deals, the BBC reports parties have until Nov. 27 to form local governments.
Haitians cheer El Salvador's troops in the fight against gangs, but the Guardian reports some fear the offensive could worsen the crisis.
Need to know: Nepal's prime minister makes his first bilateral visit to India, the BBC reports Balendra Shah is due to meet Narendra Modi in Delhi.
An Indian man gets over 19 years for plotting to kill a Sikh leader, the BBC reports India has denied involvement.
Floods worsen life in Gaza's tent camps as winter nears, the Guardian reports a collapsing sandbank killed four people near one camp.
Money & markets: Zscaler jumps 18% in extended trading on a CrowdStrike takeover report, CNBC cites Bloomberg reporting that talks are ongoing.
An early polar vortex breakdown threatens Europe's gas supply, CNBC reports storage began winter at its lowest level in over a decade.
Bitcoin fell below $62,000 on Friday morning in its latest sell-off, CNBC reports it was trading below that level.
Future frontiers: SpaceX's Cursor weighs dropping Chinese AI models, CNBC reports a House report cites geopolitical risk.
The FBI is reportedly probing a hack of its crime database, the BBC reports, citing US media.
The US, Mexico and Bolivia lose their measles free status, the Guardian reports amid low or falling vaccination rates.
The score: Lauren Price becomes undisputed welterweight champion, BBC Sport reports she won every round in Cardiff.
James Harden scores 51 as Cleveland beat Indiana 128 to 119, BBC Sport reports he passed Kobe Bryant for 50 point games.
Max Verstappen will start on pole in Las Vegas, BBC Sport reports Kimi Antonelli was fastest but has a grid penalty.
Life & culture: Fewer coins land in Rome's Trevi Fountain after a 2 euro fee, the Guardian reports a charity says its donations are down.
London's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree is felled in Norway, the BBC reports the 21m tree is about 75 years old.
Dead pets meant for cremation are found dumped in the Philippines, the BBC reports rescuers say they found 15 dumping sites near Manila.
